title: Flying-car concept (from the coupe)
brief: A two-door coupe body blocked out from photos: one smooth skinned shell (cq skin through cross-sections along z, nose at z=0, y up from the ground) with four wheel arches, plus four wheels as a second body. Every catalogue row is an envelope the body must hit: overall length, body width, roof height, ground clearance. Wheels sit on the ground and clear their arches. The flying variant adds a low main wing (NACA 2412) with a ducted lift fan through each panel and a tail stabiliser; the wingspan is a catalogue value.

checks.rule: the wheels stand on the ground (lowest point at y = 0)
every tyre clears its wheel arch by at least 20 mm
nothing hangs below the body's ground clearance
the body is a smooth skinned shell: at least 40% of its surface comes from skin()
the main wing and tail are NACA panels: at least 15% of the body's surface comes from wing()

axes: length along z (nose at z = 0), y up from the ground (y = 0), x across (width centred on x = 0)
